## EMST role: Ecologist (state variant, journey level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:relatedMatch`, confidence 0.35, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-wa:R20-ecologist/state:516K`). *Authority position (editorial):* advisor-researcher.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Assess and monitor biodiversity across species and habitats — journey L2 *(distinguishing)*
- Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference — journey L2
- Assess species habitat requirements and habitat condition — journey L2
- Recognize and assess ecosystems that have crossed into novel states — journey L2
- Plan for ecological transformation with resist, accept or direct strategies — journey L2
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — journey L2
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L1
- Read site history and reference conditions from landscape evidence — journey L2
- Identify organisms from field characters, specimens, images and recordings — journey L2
- Assess climate vulnerability of species, ecosystems, infrastructure and communities — journey L2
- Build, calibrate and validate predictive and simulation models of environmental systems — journey L2
- Assess ecosystem services with production-function models validated against observations — journey L2

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Analyze long-term biodiversity monitoring data to estimate change in occupancy or richness against conservation objectives, stating uncertainty — 6.0% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Implement a multi-taxon biodiversity monitoring protocol at assigned sites, coordinating crews, passive detectors and sample collection to schedule — 5.9% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Report biodiversity monitoring findings to decision-makers with recommended protections, separating observed change from inference and stating its limits — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Adjust the monitoring schedule or method mix at a site when disturbance, access loss or detector failure threatens the time series, recording the change — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Measure habitat attributes such as cover, structure, water and forage at used and available sites following a habitat-use study protocol — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Assess ecological function and conservation value of a novel species assemblage at a site using field indicators of structure, process and habitat — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Map potential climate refugia from topographic, hydrologic and climate data, stating the assumptions and validation of the refugia model. — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Choose the mix of field, sensor, remote-sensing and community methods for a monitoring programme from cost, detection and comparability evidence. — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Estimate treatment effects on ecological response variables with a method suited to the design, reporting effect sizes and intervals. — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Analyze trends in a long-term monitoring dataset, accounting for changes in methods, effort and detection over the record. — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Integrate habitat findings into land-use or project plans as specific measures that avoid or reduce effects on species of concern — 3.6% *(needed at entry)*
- Determine whether restoration to historical conditions is feasible at a site, documenting the thresholds, drivers and costs that limit recovery — 3.6% *(needed at entry)*
